processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot of Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C prepared in a 5 kg ingot by vacuum induction furnace, then heated to 1100 °C for 2 h.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: forged into a square forging ingot measuring 80 mm × 70 mm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot forged into a square forging ingot measuring 80 mm × 70 mm.
Forging ingot reheated to 1100 °C and held for 2 h before hot rolling.

processing_steps.temperature: initial rolling temperature approximately 1050 °C; finishing rolling temperature approximately 950 °C
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: hot rolled from 80 to 12 mm thickness in eight passes
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot rolled from 80 to 12 mm thickness in eight passes with initial rolling temperature ~1050 °C and finishing rolling temperature ~950 °C.
Hot-rolled plate air cooled to room temperature; corresponding sample labeled HR.

processing_steps.method: intercritical quenching (reheating in ferrite + austenite dual-phase region)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled plate reheated to 1050 °C, located in the ferrite and austenite dual-phase region, for 1 h; corresponding sample IQ-1050 (parent process of QA-680).
Followed by water quenching after the 1050 °C / 1 h hold, producing sample IQ-1050.
Water-quenched plate annealed for 1 h at 680 °C; corresponding sample labeled QA-680.
Annealed plate air cooled to room temperature (Fig. 1 annealing step closed by air cooling to room temperature).

structures.overall_structure: Micro-laminated (banded) microstructure retained after intercritical quenching and annealing, consisting of δ-ferrite band and tempered martensite lamellar; a large number of fine austenite grains (retained austenite after quenching plus reverted austenite) widely distributed in the tempered martensite region.
structures.microstructure_counts: dual-phase micro-laminated structure (δ-ferrite band + tempered martensite lamellar) with dispersed fine austenite grains

phases_present.morphology: coarser lath/lamellar tempered-martensite structure with reverted austenite arrowed

phases_present.volume_fraction: ~35 % (EBSD), ~37 % (XRD) total austenite including retained and reverted austenite
phases_present.morphology: blocky, coarse austenite regions distributed through the tempered martensite; fine reverted austenite grains among the tempered martensitic laths
phases_present.grain_size: ~90 % of austenite grains less than 4.8 μm; histogram peaked at <1.6 μm bin (~just below 30 % of grains)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: TAustenite grain size distribution peaked at <1.6 μm (just below 30 %), followed by 1.6–2.0 μm (~20 %), monotonic decrease to 4.4–4.8 μm bin, with a secondary rise in >4.8 μm (<10 %); ~90 % of grains <4.8 μm

phases_present.morphology: elongated light-grey δ-ferrite bands segmented/dispersed by martensite lamellar

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation accumulation at the δ-ferrite band / tempered martensite lamellar interfaces
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: During tensile tests, ductile deformation led to dislocation accumulation at the interfaces of δ-ferrite band and tempered martensite lamellar; due to the hardness difference between the two phases, stress concentration was prone to occur at their interfaces, inducing crack initiation. Cracks were captured by δ-ferrite and propagated into and along δ-ferrite band, forming second cracks; the crack could be blunted by the soft δ-ferrite phase, producing high resistance to cracking.

interfaces.slip_behavior: In stage I of work hardening, dislocation gliding started sequentially in ferrite and austenite as well as tempered martensite, according to the difference of phase hardness; large dislocation mean free path of ferrite caused the WHR to sharply decrease. Low GND density in tempered martensite promoted coordinate deformation between tempered martensite and δ-ferrite band.
interfaces.phase_evolution: After annealing, reverted austenite nucleated and grew up at martensite lath gaps; with increasing annealing temperature, increasingly reverted austenite nucleated and grew at the martensitic lath gaps, so block boundaries were gradually replaced by austenitic grain boundaries. In QA-680 no carbides precipitated (unlike QA-620).
interfaces.interface_notes: δ-ferrite and prior austenite grains grew up after the 1050 °C heating, and ferrite bands were segmented by martensite lamellar, becoming dispersed; this situation was kept in the annealed microstructure.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: rod-shaped sample size of M 10*60 mm, gauge length 25 mm; tensile axis parallel to the rolling direction of the hot-rolled plate
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Electronic tensile testing machine (WDW-100E); experimental steel could be substituted for TRIP 590T/400Y from SAE J2745-2007 standard (comparative reference)
